subject: Re: DPA - post-signature subprocessor notice & Exhibit B update
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@dataco.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@dataco.com
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Executed DPA and upcoming subprocessor additions

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for getting the DPA across the line last week — attached is our countersigned copy for your records (DataCo_Signed_DPA.pdf). We are planning a small update to Exhibit B next month to add two additional subprocessors (an analytics partner and a backup storage provider).

Before we proceed, our security team asked for:
- confirmation of the data transfer mechanisms you rely on (SCCs, encryption-in-transit, any transfers to non-EEA locations)
- an updated Exhibit B showing the new subprocessors and the regions they operate in
- whether Redwood provides proactive notice to customers when subprocessors change, and what the notice window is

Can you confirm the above and share a proposed Exhibit B for our review? We prefer execution via DocuSign for any updated exhibit.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Sr. Contracts Manager, DataCo
Attachments: DataCo_Signed_DPA.pdf

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@dataco.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Executed DPA and upcoming subprocessor additions

Maya —

Appreciate the signed DPA, and congrats on getting that across the finish line. Quick answers while we prepare an updated Exhibit B (we'll attach a draft by end of day Tuesday):

- Data transfers: Redwood relies on a combination of contractual safeguards and technical controls. For transfers from the EU/UK we use EU SCCs (standard contractual clauses) and TLS 1.2+ for in-transit encryption. Data at rest is encrypted; key management is customer-specific for Private deployments and KMS-integrated for Hosted/Dedicated.
- Regions: the two subprocessors you mentioned (analytics partner & backup storage) operate from us-west and eu-west respectively; one has limited processing in Singapore for DR purposes.
- Customer notice: Redwood's standard practice is to publish subprocessor updates to the customer portal and send email notice. We typically provide a 30-day notice window for material additions; for critical security changes we can expedite.

I'll draft Exhibit B with the new subprocessors listed, include the transfer mechanisms and region tags, and propose a clause that commits us to a 30-day notice for additions, with a right to object. Rishi and Neha — any redline/required language from legal/security we should include prior to sending?

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Executed DPA and upcoming subprocessor additions — need legal/security input

Team — forwarding DataCo note and my reply. Key asks for the Exhibit B draft: list of subprocessors (names, function, region), statement of transfer mechanism (SCCs where applicable), and a notice clause (we suggested 30 days + right to object).

Priority items for review:
1) Do we accept listing Singapore as a DR location for the backup storage provider? Any policy/controls we need to surface?
2) Proposed customer notice language (we currently say portal + email, 30 days). Legal: do we include automatic termination right if objection not resolved? Security: confirm phrasing around SCCs and KMS.

I drafted an initial Exhibit B and attached it (Exhibit-B-Subprocessors-v2.pdf). Please add redlines inline and I'll reconcile before sending to DataCo.

Thanks — Laura

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T10:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Executed DPA and upcoming subprocessor additions — need legal/security input

Thanks Laura — quick thoughts after reviewing the draft Exhibit B: 

- Acceptable to list the Singapore DR processing, but add a sentence: "Processing outside the EEA/UK will be limited to encrypted backup replication for disaster recovery; no production processing occurs in APAC without prior written consent." This limits risk.
- For transfers: confirm we reference "EU Standard Contractual Clauses (as amended)" and note that for UK exports we use the UK Addendum.
- Notice clause: keep the 30-day notice and an objection window of 15 days. If DataCo objects and we cannot reasonably mitigate, then customer may terminate affected services for the impacted dataset only (not whole agreement). That is more palatable than full termination.
- Execution: we should re-execute Exhibit B via DocuSign and attach the redlined PDF. I'll prepare a brief cover note for the envelope.

Neha — can you confirm SOC 2 link and whether we want to include an explicit "audit evidence available on request" line? Also Karthik — confirm whether our Hosted key management phrasing is accurate for this account (they are on Dedicated or Hosted?).

-rishi
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
